items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That was the beginning of a relationship that really helped me, Clement Barone.

ctx.x: No, that Sonny King, he turned out to be a preacher. A heavy-set guy. I kind of have a vision of him. Wayne told me he passed away. Sonny King, he was along with us in age. He had a flute in his attic at that time. I don’t know how I got it. He just brought it and gave it to me. I learned to play that flute to play that solo. I struggled for two days. Couldn’t get a sound out of the thing. It’s an old Bettoney flute. That was B-e-t-t – I think it was B-e-t-t-o-n-y. Maybe you haven’t ever heard of it. I don’t even…

One night, going to – the school required – music appreciation – required that we go to symphony concerts. On the way to that symphony, one of those symphony concerts, I ran into two flute players who played in the orchestra, David Covig and Clement Barone. I just went – I must have had a lot of gall to walk up to those guys, as I think back. What would make me do that? Walk up and say, “Would you give me flute lessons?” David Covig looked at Clement Barone and said, “You take him.” Just like that. That was the…
We’re going to get to him when we get to the Juilliard.
